subject: Private/VPC deployment: evidence & license scope — request and proposed redlines
messages:
From: Caroline Brooks <caroline.brooks@medtech.co>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@medtech.co>, MedTech Solutions Procurement <procurement@medtech.co>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment evidence & scope — checklist request

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. Procurement and our security reviewers have one consolidated ask before legal will sign the Order Form for the private VPC deployment. They want a concise evidence package mapped to the deployment options and to confirm the license/operator boundaries. High level:

- A table that maps every requested evidence item (logs, audit snapshots, operator access attestation, key custody) to where/how we will deliver it for the on-prem vs. VPC variants.
- Clarification of the license scope for private deploy: who is the operator (customer vs. Redwood) and whether the license permits internal switching of an operator for maintenance.
- Draft redlines to the MSA clauses about audit windows, snapshot retention, and hot/failover operator access.
- Any escrow-like pathway or proof-of-access that doesn’t require source code escrow (customer prefers operational proof only).

Can you share a matrix and proposed redlines by EOD Friday? I can pull in our security contacts if you need to confirm specifics.

Best,
Caroline Brooks
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedTech Solutions

(Attachments: customer-security-scope.pdf)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Brooks <caroline.brooks@medtech.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & scope — checklist request

Caroline — thanks for the clear list. We can do a mapping matrix and a short set of MSA redlines focused specifically on operational evidence and license boundary language. Quick notes:

- We generally avoid source-code escrow; we can offer automated snapshot proofs, signed attestations of access, and audited runbooks.
- For "operator" definition, we typically ship operator credentials to the customer for private/on-prem and provide a managed-operator option (Redwood-managed) under a separate exhibit with explicit SLA/maintenance windows.
- We'll produce two artifacts: (1) Evidence matrix (spreadsheet) and (2) Compact redline doc for MSA + Order Form.

Laura — can you take the lead on the MSA redlines? Priya — can you draft the evidence matrix with the delivery modalities? I’ll own the responses to Caroline and MedTech procurement.

Michael Grant
Director, Partnerships (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: none)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & scope — checklist request

Michael / Priya — looping legal in. I reviewed Caroline's bullets and sketched the redlines in the attached doc. Summary of my approach:

- Narrow the audit window language to a mutually agreed calendar window (e.g., 30-day advance notice for non-emergency on-site audits; 48-hour notice for remote log pulls unless a legal hold is in place).
- Provide an explicit exhibit describing operator roles: "Customer-Operated" (default for private/VPC) vs. "Redwood-Managed" (optional, additional fees). Include a requirement that any temporary access for maintenance be logged, time-limited, and subject to customer approval for scope.
- For snapshot proofs: propose a signed hash timeline (timestamped snapshots of a minimal operational artifact, stored in an integrity-protected bucket) rather than code escrow. This satisfies customers who need proof of operational access without source code escrow.

I added inline comments to sections 7 (Audit; Inspection Rights) and 12 (License; Deployment Rights). I flagged two negotiation hotspots for you, Michael:

1) Customer wants retention of "audit snapshots" for 3 years — we should push back to 12 months unless there's a compelling regulatory reason.
2) They asked for the right to "switch operator" at will — we can allow operator transition with 30 days' notice and predefined handover procedures, not unilateral immediate switch.

Attached: redline_msa_2026-08-11.docx (draft).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Transactions
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redline_msa_2026-08-11.docx)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & scope — checklist request

Team — attached is the evidence matrix. Highlights and proposed delivery paths:

- Audit logs: we can deliver redacted log slices (sufficient to show operator actions) via a time-limited signed S3 link for VPC. For on-prem, we provide an ingestion guide + schema and an automated export tool run by the customer; we can also run an integrity scan on request.
- Operator access attestation: a signed access log export (we can generate a PDF attestation with an HSM-backed signature for Redwood-managed operator actions).
- Snapshot proofs: we will produce timestamped SHA-256 hashes of a minimal runtime artifact and publish the hashes to a customer-shared, time-stamped ledger (Drive + signed manifest).
- Evidence delivery cadence: initial evidence bundle at Go-Live, then quarterly exports for the first year unless otherwise negotiated.

I included internal owners column and an estimated lead time per item in the XLSX. Rishi — I left two security questions for you (HSM vs. KMS cryptographic signing and whether we should offer a standing SOC2 attestation upload).

Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: priv-deploy-evidence-matrix.xlsx)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Brooks <caroline.brooks@medtech.co>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@medtech.co>, MedTech Solutions Procurement <procurement@medtech.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence & scope — checklist request

Caroline / Evan — attaching two deliverables per your ask: (1) an evidence matrix that maps each requested item to how we will deliver it for both VPC (customer-managed) and on-prem deployments, and (2) a compact set of MSA redlines focused on audit windows, operator roles, and snapshot proofing.

Key callouts in plain English:
- Operator model: Default is Customer-Operated for private/VPC. If you elect Redwood-Managed, we will run maintenance under an Exhibit with defined maintenance windows and access logging.
- Audit snapshots: We propose signed timestamped hashes retained for 12 months by default; extendable to 36 months by exception with fees or regulatory need.
- Audit access: remote log exports with 48-hour notice for urgent investigations; 30-day notice for routine audits. On-site audits are permitted with 30 days' notice and scoped agenda.

Next steps: If this aligns, can you confirm which operator model you intend to select and whether MedTech requires 36 months retention as a hard requirement? Once we get that, Laura will produce a negotiation-ready MSA and we can send the Order Form with the appropriate Exhibit.

Thanks — I’ll remain the point of contact for contract coordination.

Michael Grant
Director, Partnerships (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: priv-deploy-evidence-matrix.xlsx; redline_msa_2026-08-11.docx)
